quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must proceed slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then proceed when the way is clear.
You must stop, then proceed when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the red arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop, then proceed when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and wait until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: What should you do to prepare for hazards ahead?

options.text: Keep looking at the entire road and roadsides.
Look straight ahead only.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep looking at the entire road and roadsides.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better by finding and spotting problems early. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look far ahead and scan the entire road, including the sides.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when there is a passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes going the same way. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for traffic when returning to the road.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let pedestrians and other traffic clear the intersection.

questions.question: You are angry after an incident at work. When you reach your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly to not think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, calm down before driving. Letting emotions affect your driving is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season for driving.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show where the road curves. The arrow points in the direction of the curve. Multiple chevron signs may appear along the curve.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to other vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: How does the type of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment. The type does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use loudspeakers to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions they give over their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if you are driving slowly and causing traffic to back up, you must pull off the road to let others pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle using the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcyclists a complete lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, motorcyclists need space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What can reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.
Replace tires with bad tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on top of water between the tires and the road. Low air pressure, bad tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What is true about larger vehicles?

options.text: They have larger blind spots.
They have smaller blind spots.
They have no blind spots.
They have the same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight.
You may only drive in the direction of the arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction shown by the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when a driver does not see another vehicle or does something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: Yield to the driver on your right when you both arrive at the same time. Wait until it is safe, then proceed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: Faster speeds reduce your tires' ability to remove water from the road. At high speeds, your tires may hydroplane and slide on a film of water instead of gripping the road.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: Yield to the vehicle on your right. Wait until it is safe, then you may proceed.

questions.question: Which must you obey above all others?

options.text: A steady red light.
A police officer.
A stop sign.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take precedence over all traffic signs and signals. This includes police officers, fire police, highway work zone flaggers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On hills or curves because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow.
White.
Red.
Black.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction and mark the road's right edge. Broken white lines may be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up to get in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a cyclist and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers and should not be crowded. Passing too quickly can knock them off-course.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Never drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect light back at you and reduce visibility even more.

questions.question: How should you look to reduce headlight glare at night?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers do not dim their lights, look to the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look at the headlights, as the glare can blind you temporarily.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Always keep your current speed.
Speed up to avoid congestion.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: Make room for entering traffic when you are on a multi-lane road. Move over one lane if the next lane is clear.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to the original lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. Trees and buildings block the sun. These areas also take longer to dry in wet weather.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is signaling to enter the main road after loading or unloading passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.
